speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: The Attorney-General's Chamber (AGC) made a Reference to the Court of Appeal on the City Harvest Church Case.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: I want to set out the Government's position, now that the Court of Appeal has said what the law is.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: The key question is related to the liability of company directors, governing board members, key officers of charities and officers of societies.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: When they commit criminal breach of trust (CBT) or property which belongs to the organisation, what happens?

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: Section 409 provides for a maximum of life imprisonment.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: If you are a senior officer, director in the organisation, you are in a position of greater trust.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: You have considerable authority to make decisions in relation to the organisation’s assets.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: If you abuse that trust, you should be more culpable and should be liable for more severe punishments, compared with an ordinary employee.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: That is really common sense and there can be no question about that.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: For the last 40 years, the law, as applied by the Courts, reflected this principle.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: In 1976, the High Court ruled so in the case of Tay Choo Wah.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: It said that directors are liable for the aggravated offence provided under section 409.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: After that decision, the position was clear, settled law.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: The law was applied in that way for over 40 years, by Courts in other cases.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: There are at least 16 decisions – reported – applying this principle and there must be many other unreported decisions.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: In April last year, however, the position changed.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: The High Court ruled that directors cannot be liable under section 409.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: That was contrary to the decision in 1976 and the way the Courts have applied section 409 over these 40 years.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: The Government asked AGC what should be done, what further steps ought to be taken after the High Court's ruling.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: AGC advised that a clarification should be sought from the Court of Appeal by way of a Reference.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: We now have two conflicting positions from the High Court.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: One, Tay Choo Wah and the line of cases that applied Tay Choo Wah.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: And second, the City Harvest Church case where the Court disagreed with Tay Choo Wah.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: The Court of Appeal gave its decision, as I said earlier, last Thursday in response to the two questions of law submitted by AGC.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: As it stands today, ordinary employees can be charged under section 408 of the Penal Code.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: That provides for more serious penalties for CBT compared with section 408.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: It is punishable by mandatory imprisonment for up to 15 years, and an optional fine.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: Directors, however, can only be charged under section 406 – which provides for a lesser punishment up to seven years’ jail or fine or both.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: The Court of Appeal itself acknowledged this gap in the law and it said that there was no "good policy reason" to ignore the “heightened culpability” of directors and key officers of charities, societies and companies who commit CBT.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: The Court of Appeal also pointed out that the obligation of the Court is to set out the legal position correctly on what the law says, and to leave it to Parliament to amend the law as it deems fit.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: We hope to make the amendment, together with the other wide-ranging amendments to the Penal Code, which I have spoken about.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: To the House, let me make one final comment – we are aware that many have expressed their dissatisfaction with the outcome.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: Expressing one’s unhappiness with Court decisions is fine, but it should not sink to the level of abuse, insults and contempt.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: We have seen comments online that the judges let off those who are rich; that some judges were lenient because they were Christians, and so on.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: Judges should not be personally attacked and their integrity impugned, just because people do not agree with their decision.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: People are entitled to disagree with their decision.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: The Government believes that the sentences are too low but the sentences reflect the law, as it stands, after the High Court's decision last year and confirmed by the Court of Appeal.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: All of us have to respect the decision, regardless of whether we agree or disagree with it.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: As rightly pointed out, I also personally received a lot of feedback.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: On the ground, people are commenting that the Court let those who are rich go lightly and also those who can get off for religious reasons.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: The worst is they also commented that, for this particular case, it was handled by a so-called lawyer who is also a Member of Parliament (MP) from the People's Action Party (PAP).

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: So, may I know what is the Minister's stand on this and a clarification on his comments?

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Also, what can the Government do about all these comments and also how should we proceed from here?

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: I think Mr Edwin Tong would not be entirely happy to be called "a so-called lawyer and MP".

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: I think he is a qualified lawyer and a Senior Counsel.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: I said earlier that it is entirely legitimate to express one's unhappiness about Court decisions.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: But some statements have, indeed, gone too far, abusing the judges personally, ascribing improper ulterior motives to their decision.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: And it is, really, a clear case of abusing the anonymity of the Net or anonymity to the extent that it exists.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: Just because you do not agree with the judges does not mean that you have the right to abuse them and challenge their integrity.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: I will set out later some factors which will be relevant in this context.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: The Courts should not be pressured by public opinion.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: They should be free to decide in accordance with what they believe the law to be.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: Criminal cases must be tried in a Court of law, not in the court of public opinion.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: A few years ago, I already expected that there would be more and more of such scurrilous attacks on the judiciary.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: One of those opposing it, I think, it was Mr Leon Perera who asked me in this House why the need for this law.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: If we do nothing, it will get much worse and become unsolvable.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: We do not want to end up like the United Kingdom (UK) where the press freely attacks the judiciary.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: You get newspaper headlines screaming banner headlines labelling judges as "enemies of the people", "you fools" because the courts have the temerity to decide in a way that the media did not like.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: If we are not careful, we will easily go down that route.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: There is a public Facebook group with a Chinese name which I understand can be translated as a "policy discussion forum".

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: I was informed that a copy of a news article was posted on 2 February, last week, on this Facebook.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: The article had appeared in the Chinese news daily Wanbao on the same day.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: It was a report on the City Harvest Church matter.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: The original title translated was, and I quote, "Outdated laws saved the accused from harsher penalties".

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: AGC takes the view that the suggestion from the fake title is that the PAP MP was responsible for an unfair, unjust outcome and the Courts have let off the defendants lightly because of him.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: I do not want to go into the meanings of the fake title because the matter is with AGC and it will be dealt with in accordance with the law.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: Whatever the meaning of the statement and regardless of whether or not it is in contempt, one can see that this sort of attack based on deliberate faking is quite unacceptable.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: I cannot see how any reasonable person will justify such faking as a legitimate expression of free speech.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: I have asked the Police to take a serious view of those who scandalise the Court.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: If there are other comments which cross the threshold and are in contempt of the Court, our approach is that action will be taken.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: That has been so before the Administration of Justice (Protection) Act, or AOJP, and it remains so after the AOJP.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: In coming to a decision whether to prosecute for scandalising the Courts, the factors will include assessing who said it, how seriously is the statement likely to be taken, how wide was the publication, other relevant factors.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: That has always been the case, even before the AOJP.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: AGC will assess the various statements that have come to their notice in this context.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: And quite apart from whether the fake headlines scandalised the Court, there is another point.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: Defendants are entitled to get a lawyer of their choice.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: Rule of law, a civilised system of having trials in Court depends, amongst other things, on lawyers being able to act for defendants, whatever offences the defendants are accused of.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: As I have said before several times, even a child rapist is entitled to his day in Court and to be defended.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: It does not mean that we or the lawyer defending the person approves of child rape.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: But the defendant has a right to choose a lawyer to defend him, and we must not take that away from him.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: Lawyers should not be made to feel that they will be hounded online if they take up cases.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: I am probably in the unique position in Singapore of someone who has both acted for the three Prime Ministers of Singapore and also of having acted against all three of them.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: In 1995, Prime Minister Goh, Senior Minister Lee and Deputy Prime Minister Lee, as they were then, sued the International Herald Tribune (IHT) for libel.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: The conversation as to whether I would act for them took about two minutes.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: I told them they must know I was a PAP MP, and were they comfortable that they would get the best possible advice from me, given my position?

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: They knew that I was a PAP MP.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: They said it was okay with them, if it was okay with me.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: I did not see any need to clear with the Party or anyone connected to the Party or Government.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: By taking on the case, I was simply doing my professional duty.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: I did not need to take on the brief.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: I was very busy with other work but I thought the IHT had a right to counsel of its choice.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: They were faced, obviously, with particularly formidable plaintiffs who could get counsel of their choice, and so, I should help the IHT.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: The import of my acting for the IHT, when it went to Court, did not escape Senior Minister Lee Kuan Yew.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: In Court, after his evidence was over and before he stepped out of the witness box, he said he had to point out the situation.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: He said that I was close to the three of them, meaning the Prime Minister, Senior Minister and Deputy Prime Minister.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: Over the years, I also acted for various others whose conduct will not be approved of by the general public and some of whom were impecunious and could not pay fees.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: I acted for them whenever I could, based on certain principles which I do not need to go into here.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: By action here, I do not necessarily just mean contempt action.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: I mentioned that there are at least 16 reported decisions in the books confirming that decision over the years.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: No doubts or uncertainty were expressed by our Courts; prosecution, defence, everyone proceeded on that basis.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: There was no suggestion that the law was in need of any review.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: There was, therefore, no reason for Parliament to review the position or amend the law.

speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing (Chua Chu Kang)
text: One key fact of this whole City Harvest case is that a key beneficiary, which is, the wife of Kong Hee, was not charged for any offence.

speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing (Chua Chu Kang)
text: In reviewing the law, would the Ministry also look at whether to put in some penalties where the beneficiary of a CBT case can also be charged under the law?

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: I think one has to be careful about this.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: A beneficiary who receives proceeds without the appropriate knowledge does not automatically become a criminal.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: Supposing the person took the money and donated it to another charity, does the recipient commit a criminal offence?

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: But knowing receipt of property to the extent that it needs to be criminalised, you will find it in the law.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
text: Will this case have a big impact on future cases, especially between now and the time the law is changed?

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: For the cases which are being investigated, where AGC is considering the charges, again obviously, the AGC would have to take into account the decision by the Court of Appeal.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: If there are any charges to be brought in respect of actions that have taken place before any legislative changes, I am sure AGC will take into account what the appropriate charge is.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: It does not automatically mean that any changes will not apply.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: I do not want to go into those things but I think we identified a lacuna.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: I mean, it has been identified for us.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh
text: Since it has been practised for so long, it has been consistently practised, why did the Court suddenly change the precedent?

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh
text: We should follow the precedent and change should be thereafter.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Can I just remind Members, we are not here to question the specific decisions of the Court.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: I will send the copy of the judgment to Mr Gan offline because it is 150 pages or more.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: It could not have been the intention of the drafters to deal with the directors, because Company Law had not been developed to the extent that it has now.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: And therefore, it could not have been within the minds and the drafting intention.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: Therefore, you would need new provisions which deal with it.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: The other approach is to say, "Well, you take those words and you apply it as circumstances evolve".

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: They also explained why they did not want to do that here.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: That is in two lines; I am probably not doing full justice to it but that is the sense.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: If I may just remind Members, do read the Standing Orders with regard to comments, especially Standing Orders 21(1)(h) and 59, in future, on any discussions relating to issues like this.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: The Clerk will now proceed to read the Orders of the Day.
